chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Najran from 'Asim ibn Humayd from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him saying that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent to Safwan ibn Umayyah and borrowed from him seventy coats of mail with their neckpieces. He asked, 'Is it forcibly, O Muhammad?' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) replied, 'No, it is a loan with guarantee.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal distinction between a forced taking and a guaranteed loan in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the legal distinction between a forced seizure (*ghasb*) and a voluntary loan (*‘ariyyah*) with a guarantee (*daman*), as narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS). It highlights the Prophet’s practice of borrowing military equipment from prominent companions, establishing that the borrower assumes liability for loss or damage, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence regarding temporary loans.

en.sarwar: 10. Ali has narrated from his father from ibn abu Najran from ‘ Asim ibn Humayd from abu Basir who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, sent a message to Safwan ibn ‘Umayyah asking him to borrow seventy pieces of coats of arms with their helmets. He asked, ‘Is it forcibly, O Muhammad?’ The Holy Prophet replied, ‘It is borrowing with guarantee to return.’”
